newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DALY, CITING FATIGUE, WITHDRAWS FROM U.S. OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DALY, CITING FATIGUE, WITHDRAWS FROM U.S. OPEN.

text.p: John Daly, the troubled golfer who has been trying to recover from alcohol and gambling problems, withdrew from the U.S. Open Friday, citing mental and physical fatigue.

Daly, who shot seven-over-par 77 in Thursday's first round of the Open at Congressional Country Club, played the first nine holes of his second round in three over par early Friday morning before suddenly walking off the course.

He later issued a statement through his new sponsor, Callaway Golf, saying he was unable to continue playing in the Open due to a combination of mental and physical exhaustion following his latest treatment for alcoholism.
"Even though I thought I was going to be strong enough to come right back and play three straight weeks on tour, I found out that I was wrong," Daly, 31, said in the statement.
"I just started feeling real weak after a few holes today, and by the time I got to number nine, I was physically exhausted," he added.

Daly, winner of the 1995 British Open and the 1991 PGA Championship, underwent eight weeks of substance abuse treatment in April and May after an alcohol-related incident on March 27 in his hotel room during the Players Championship -- after a night of drinking.
He also withdrew from that event and subsequently underwent the treatment at the Betty Ford Clinic in Palm Springs, Calif.
That episode cost Daly several lucrative endorsement contracts but he has since signed with Callaway -- with the understanding that he continues counselling.

In the statement Callaway issued after Daly withdrew from the Open, company founder and chairman Ely Callaway expressed his continuing support for Daly, still one of the most popular personalities in golf.
"Championship golf tournaments create the ultimate in emotional stress and physical hardship for even the healthiest athelete," said Callaway, whose company makes the popular Big Bertha clubs.

"We feel that John Daly showed his remarkable qualities in making the cut at the Memorial Tournament and the Kemper Open on successive weeks, and that he was simply trying to do too much too soon by playing three straight weeks --especially under U.S. Open conditions," Callaway added.

Daly's stint at the Betty Ford Clinic was the second time that Daly had undergone treatment for alcohol abuse since he burst on the golf scene with a surprising victory in the '91 PGA at Crooked Stick in Carmel, Indiana.
The golfer said in the statement that he intended to take "several weeks" off from golf, during which he will begin a physical fitness programme.
"I'm looking forward to coming back to play competitive golf when I'm healthy and physically prepared," Daly said, adding that he appreciated all the support he has recived from his fans.
